description: The reference answers Fuaran.Compute.DataFrameConformance.transformLaws compares a host evaluator against, over a sample declared by `seed` and `iterations` and computed by calling Fuaran.Compute.DataFrame.evalPipeline. `input.source` is a canonical DataSource wire string (an Embedded table) and `input.pipeline` a canonical Transform pipeline wire string — both decode with the host's existing dataframe codec; no new codec is needed. A host runs the family by decoding both, evaluating the pipeline with ITS OWN evaluator, and comparing: an `ok` vector requires the host's result table to encode byte-for-byte to `expected.table`, and an `error` vector requires the host to refuse the pipeline too. The refusal is unnamed unless the vector carries `expected.error` — the parity contract compares that both sides errored, never which error, so a host must not gate on a class this file does not carry. To reproduce the sample rather than replay it: per iteration draw intBelow(4) = extra (rows = extra + 2) and intBelow(7) = offset, then build columns g = Str of [a;b;c][i mod 3], v = Null when (i + offset) mod 4 = 0 else Int(i*3 + offset - 5), and w = Float((i + offset) / 2). The pipeline shape is the iteration index modulo eight over the shapes named in each vector id — a fixed cycle rather than a draw, so no shape can be missed. From iteration 16 each iteration takes the next DECIMAL shape named in its id over the same two draws, with rows = extra + 3 and columns g as above; m = Decimal, null when (i + offset) mod 4 = 3, else ((i*137 + offset*25) mod 500 - 200) hundredths; v = Int(i*2 - offset); w = Float((i + offset) / 4). A second operand table, where a shape takes one, is the same build over rows - 1 rows. These are BEHAVIOUR vectors: a host asserts the encoded result, not the framing of this file. After the evalPipeline vectors come two further case kinds (Phase 321), each a reference answer over hand-declared inputs: `columnOp` vectors carry `input.source` (an embedded table) and `input.op` (a canonical ColumnOp wire string); a host applies the op and compares as for evalPipeline (`expected.table` on `ok`, a refusal on `error`), and re-encodes its decode of `input.op` to `expected.op`. `delta` vectors carry `input.before`, `input.after` and `input.key`; a host diffs the two tables keyed by that column's cell token and encodes the delta to `expected.delta`. `iterations` counts the evalPipeline vectors only. From the iteration after the last decimal shape, each takes the next TYPING shape named in its vector id (Phase 338) over the decimal table: a derived or unpivoted column is typed by its expression where the schema decides it, over an empty and an all-null frame alike, and a float beside a decimal in one derived column is refused. From the iteration after the last typing shape, each takes the next UNIT shape named in its vector id (Phase 429) over the unit table — rows = extra + 3; g as above; d = Int((i+1)*100 + offset*10) in metres (label Distance), null when (i + offset) mod 4 = 3; t = Float((i+1+offset)*2.5) in seconds, null when (i + offset) mod 5 = 4; h = Float(i + offset + 0.5) in seconds; w = Float((i*3 + offset)/4) in kilograms; dk = d/1000 as Float in kilometres; n = Int(i + offset), unitless, label Count, description How many; the second operand of a join or a set verb is the same build over rows - 1 rows (the union refusal's declares d in kilometres): a column's unit, label and description ride every verb that keeps a column, a derive carries the unit the check derives and a conversion resolves to a float, an aggregate and a window keep their source's unit or carry none, and two units met where the rule requires one are refused. From the iteration after the last unit shape, each takes the next REPEAT shape named in its vector id (Phase 468) over the decimal table: a project, a group-by, an unpivot and a pivot whose output would name one column twice are refused. From the iteration after the last repeat shape, each takes the next POWER shape named in its vector id (Phase 557) over the decimal table. Every power vector is BYTE-EXACT on every host (Phase 594): an integer-exponent `pow` runs one pinned routine, binary exponentiation over IEEE-754 multiplication with one reciprocal for a negative exponent, equal bit for bit to the repeated-multiplication spelling up to the cube; every row of the special-value table (`pow(0,0)`, `pow(1,y)`, `pow(0,negative)`, a negative base under a non-integer exponent, `ln` at and below zero, `ln 1`, `exp` underflow) is answered before any routine; and a float-exponent `pow`, `exp`, `ln` and `log10` run the pinned routines of `Fuaran.Compute.LinearAlgebra.Elementary` (fdlibm's reductions and coefficients in `+ - * /` and comparisons, `pow` as `exp(y * ln x)` in double-double, published with their own vectors in `linear-algebra-laws.json`), so a host transcribes those routines and matches the recorded bits. A vector whose output the reference's static walk marks HOST-ROUNDED — none in this file since Phase 594 — carries `expected.tolerance`, an object naming each such output column with the bound in ULPS a host's value may sit from the recorded one, the distance between two doubles being the difference of their IEEE-754 binary64 bit patterns read as ordered integers (a negative double's pattern reflected below zero, so adjacent doubles are one apart). A host compares a named column cell by cell — one type, one length, null in the same rows, each pair of present nonzero finite floats of one sign within the bound, a zero of either sign, a non-finite float and any other cell equal exactly — and the rest of the table byte for byte: its answer with every named column replaced by the recorded one encodes to `expected.table` exactly (Phase 559). A host that does not implement the four functions reports the power vectors as unsupported and never skips them silently. A pinned column is never named, so a vector without the member is compared byte for byte. From the iteration after the last power shape, each takes the next OVERFLOW shape named in its vector id (Phase 572) over the decimal table: `add`, `sub`, `mul` and an integer-exponent `pow` over int32 operands, each first derived into a column so the operation runs over a column. An integer result is range-checked against the int32 band, never wrapped and never widened: a `-refused` vector's result lies past one edge of the band (above it, or below it), and the host must refuse it with the class `expected.error` names, `OverflowError`; an `-in-band` vector lands on or beside the band's edges and must be answered, not refused. A host that computes over a wider integer, an unbounded integer or an IEEE-754 double must check the result against the band before answering. From the iteration after the last overflow shape, each takes the next ORDERING shape named in its vector id (Phase 584) over the decimal table: a key a `sort`, a `sort` followed by a `limit`, or a `window`'s partition or order takes from the pipeline is a column reference, resolved against the step's input schema before any row is read, and a key that names no column is refused with the class `expected.error` names, `UnknownColumn` — never the input order returned as if it had been sorted, nor one partition answered as if it were several; each refusal has an in-schema neighbour that must be answered. From the iteration after the last ordering shape, each takes the next UNION shape named in its vector id over the decimal table, projected to `g` and `v` renamed `x`, against a second operand of rows - 1 rows carrying `g` and one column the shape declares (x = Int(i*5 - 3), Float(i + 0.5) or Str of i, or y = Int(i*5 - 3) for the name mismatch): a pair of one type unions under that type, an int beside a float unions as a float, a pair no column type holds together (a string beside an int) is refused as `TypeError`, and sides whose column names differ are refused as `JoinError`. After the function and curve shapes, each iteration takes the next FIT shape named in its vector id (Phase 592) over a fixed ten-row table carried whole in `input.source`: ordinary least squares by the streaming Givens QR of the linear-algebra package, so every estimate, standard error and statistic is pinned bytes; an aliased column is named with null estimates, a decimal response's fitted values, residuals and deviances are decimal, and a response outside its family or a non-finite term is refused as `FitError`. After the fit shapes, each iteration takes the next PREDICT shape named in its vector id (Phase 597) over the same table, which is also each model's training rows: the appended `predicted`, `se_fit`, `se_pred`, `lower` and `upper` are pinned bytes — a row's prediction is its fitted value, the standard errors one triangular solve and a sum of squares, and an interval's quantile a row of the t table read by `Interpolate` — and an untabled level, a prediction interval outside the gaussian family, a level or a group the model does not hold and a term a coefficient table lacks are each refused as `FitError`. After the predict shapes, each iteration takes the next FAMILY shape named in its vector id (Phase 598) over the same table: quasi-Poisson (Poisson's iterations, Pearson's dispersion) and Tweedie at p = 1.5 (working weights w·μ^(2−p) through the pinned pow) under the log link, and the sandwich standard errors HC0 to HC3 in a fit's `std_error` and `t` — one pass over the rows in a pinned order — all pinned bytes; a Tweedie power between zero and one, a response outside Tweedie's range, robust errors beside a ridge penalty and a prediction from a robust model are refused as `FitError`. After the family shapes, each iteration takes the next GENERAL GLM shape named in its vector id (Phase 600) over the same table: the binomial under the logit, probit and cloglog links, quasi-binomial, a weighted proportion, Poisson under the identity and square-root links, Gamma under the inverse link, inverse Gaussian under the inverse-square link, Gaussian under the log link and the negative binomial with θ fixed and estimated (its `theta`, `theta_std_error` and `alternations`), all pinned bytes through the pinned erfc, normal and elementary functions; predictions on the response scale map an interval's ends through the inverse link; a separated outcome is refused as `OverflowError`, and a mean below its range, a θ with no estimate and a prediction with no mean as `FitError`.
